instructions: The marks are indicated in the right-hand margin.
There are NINE questions in this paper.

questions.text: Choose the correct alternative from any seven of the following :

sub_questions.text: The current through $2 \Omega$ resistor is: [Diagram: A circuit with a $3 \Omega$ resistor in series with a $5 \text{ V}$ source. Then a parallel branch with a $4 \Omega$ resistor and a $4 \text{ A}$ current source. Then a $2 \Omega$ resistor and a $4V_3$ dependent voltage source. $V_3$ is the voltage across the $3 \Omega$ resistor.]

A $500 \text{ V}$, 3-phase induction motor has an output of $50 \text{ hp}$ and operates at a power factor of $0.85$ lagging with an efficiency of $90\%$. The readings of the two wattmeters respectively are:

A coil takes $2.5 \text{ A}$ when connected across $200 \text{ V}$, $50 \text{ Hz}$ mains. The power consumed by the coil is found to be $400 \text{ W}$. The coil inductance and power factor respectively are:
Which among the following is/are the main characteristic(s) of a fuse element?

A resistance, a condenser and a variable inductance are connected in series across a $200 \text{ V}$, $50 \text{ Hz}$ supply. The maximum current which can be obtained by varying the inductance under resonance is $314 \text{ mA}$ and the voltage across the condenser is then $300 \text{ V}$. The values of R-L-C respectively are:

Three similar coils, each of resistance $20 \Omega$ and inductance of $0.5 \text{ H}$, are connected in delta to a 3-phase, $50 \text{ Hz}$, $400 \text{ V}$ supply. The line current and total powers absorbed respectively are:

A 440/110 transformer has an effective primary resistance of $0.3 \Omega$ and secondary resistance of $0.02 \Omega$. Its iron losses at normal input are $150 \text{ W}$. What would be the secondary current at which the maximum efficiency will occur?
For high current and low voltage rating, which winding is employed to DC machine?
When the mechanical power developed by a DC motor is maximum:
options: back emf is equal to applied voltage
iron losses are equal to copper losses
back emf is equal to half of the applied voltage
back emf is equal to zero

sub_questions.text: In two-wattmeter method of power measurement, if one of the wattmeters gives negative reading, then it can be concluded that the load:

The efficiency of a $1000 \text{ kVA}$, $110/220 \text{ V}$, $50 \text{ Hz}$, single-phase transformer is $98.5\%$ at half full-load at $0.8 \text{ pf}$ leading and $98.8\%$ at full-load upf. Determine— (i) iron-loss; (ii) full-load copper loss; (iii) maximum efficiency at upf; (iv) kVA at which maximum efficiency occurs.

In a $440 \text{ V}$, $50 \text{ c/s}$ transformer, the total iron loss is $2500 \text{ W}$. When the applied voltage is $220 \text{ V}$ at $25 \text{ c/s}$, the corresponding loss is $850 \text{ W}$. Calculate the eddy-current loss at normal frequency and voltage.

A 3-$\phi$, 4-pole, $50 \text{ Hz}$, star-connected induction motor running on full-load develops a useful torque of $300 \text{ N-m}$. The rotor EMF is completing 120 cycles per minute. If torque lost in friction is $50 \text{ N-m}$, calculate— (i) slip; (ii) net output power; (iii) mechanical power developed; (iv) rotor copper losses/phase; (v) rotor efficiency; (vi) rotor resistance per phase if rotor current is $60 \text{ A}$ in running condition.
Explain the torque speed characteristics of 3-phase induction motor by considering the zones of operation.

A $440 \text{ V}$, 3-$\phi$, 8-pole, $50 \text{ Hz}$, $400 \text{ kW}$, star-connected induction motor has the following parameters : Stator resistance = $0.1 \Omega$, Stator reactance = $0.4 \Omega$, Equivalent rotor resistance referred to stator = $0.15 \Omega$, Equivalent rotor reactance referred to stator = $0.44 \Omega$. The stator core loss is $1250 \text{ W}$ while mechanical loss is $1000 \text{ W}$. It draws a no-load current of $20 \text{ A}$ at a pf of $0.09$ lagging. While at a speed of $727.5 \text{ RPM}$, calculate— (i) input line current and pf; (ii) torque developed; (iii) mechanical power developed; (iv) efficiency. Use approximate equivalent circuit.
Explain the operating principle of alternator.

Find the value of R such that $1 \text{ A}$ would flow in it for the network shown in the following figure : [Diagram: A bridge/ladder circuit. On the left, a $10 \Omega$ resistor in parallel with a branch containing a $1 \Omega$ resistor and a $12 \text{ V}$ battery. Then a top branch with resistor R. Then a parallel branch with a $6 \Omega$ resistor and a $2 \Omega$ resistor on the right.]

Find the resistance between terminals x and y from the following figure : [Diagram: A complex bridge circuit with resistors $1.3 \Omega, 13 \Omega, 5 \Omega, 4.7 \Omega, 4.5 \Omega$ and inner resistors $3.25 \Omega, 1.5 \Omega, 2.5 \Omega, 1 \Omega$.]
A $4 \text{ mH}$ inductor is connected in series with a $230 \text{ V}$ sinusoidal $50 \text{ Hz}$ supply. Find peak, RMS and average values of current and power consumed.
Explain the effect of power factor on two wattmeter readings in a two-wattmeter method of power measurement.

A steel ring has a diameter of $20 \text{ cm}$, a cross-section of $25 \text{ cm}^2$ and radial air-gap of $0.8 \text{ mm}$ cut across it. When excited by a current of $1 \text{ A}$ through a coil of 1000 turns wound on the ring core, it produces an air-gap flux of $1 \text{ mWb}$. Neglecting leakage and fringing, calculate (i) relative permeability of steel and (ii) total reluctance of the magnetic circuit.
What are the various ferromagnetic materials? Write their applications and properties.
Explain the terms 'fringing' and 'leakage flux'.
Describe the various types of batteries.
Define the following terms : (i) Switch fuse unit (ii) MCB (iii) ELCB (iv) MCCB.

What value of equivalent resistance exists between points A and B? [Diagram: A large resistor network. Top branch A-B has resistors $2\Omega, 3\Omega, 4\Omega$. Vertical branches have $2\Omega, 6\Omega, 6\Omega, 2\Omega$. Horizontal internal branches have $2\Omega, 5\Omega, 5\Omega$. Bottom branch has $3\Omega$.]
Draw the resonance curve for a series resonance circuit and compare with it a parallel resonance.
